title: Tenant attestation scheduled packages with verifiable manifests
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Objective: build a tenant-facing scheduled delivery feature that produces tamper-evident attestation packages (PDF/CSV payloads + signed manifest) for compliance and audit needs. Packages must be region-aware (data residency tags), enforce retention rules at generation time, and support push and pull delivery modes (SFTP, customer cloud storage, secure download links). Motivation: customers ask for cryptographically verifiable evidence packages they can store offline and ingest into third-party GRC systems; current exports are ad-hoc and lack signed manifests and built-in residency verification.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduled package job can be created in Console with: schedule cadence, region residency filter, retention window, output formats (PDF, CSV) and delivery destination (SFTP, S3/GCS, secure download).
Each package includes a manifest.json.gz listing objects, SHA256 checksums, total record counts, residency tags, generation timestamp, and a detached signature produced using Customer or Redwood KMS.
Tenant can verify integrity: SDK CLI or Console verification shows manifest signature valid and checksums match payloads.
Retention rules are applied: records outside tenant retention windows are excluded at generation and logged in an audit entry.
Delivery retries, chunking for payloads > 1GB, and resumable upload mechanism are operational with monitoring and SLA telemetry.
Audit trail: job lifecycle events (scheduled, running, succeeded, failed, delivered) appear in tenant audit logs with links to manifests and delivery receipts.
Console: UI for schedule creation, history view, download link for recent packages, and per-job cost estimate shown before confirmation.
Compliance QA: internal security review completed and penetration checklist passed before GA.
engineering_notes: Implementation approach: generator service will run per-region workers to enforce data residency and to apply retention filters before materializing exports. Manifests created atomically and signed using Redwood KMS; option to use customer-managed KMS keys for enterprise tenants.

Trade-offs: signing manifests at generation time increases latency but is required for tamper-evidence. To mitigate, use streaming packaging where checksums are computed incrementally and manifest is finalized at end.
Storage & cost: large tenants will incur staging storage; implement TTL for staging buckets and streaming direct-to-destination where supported (e.g., S3 multipart uploads).
Security: encrypt payloads at rest with tenant-specific keys; for SFTP deliveries, support user-specific SSH keys and one-time credentials.
Compatibility: support PDF for human-readable audit bundles and CSV for machine ingestion. PDFs should include a one-page summary with manifest fingerprint and signature metadata.
qa_plan: Unit tests for manifest generation and checksum correctness.
E2E test: schedule job -> generate package -> verify signature via CLI -> compare checksums.
Failure injection: simulate destination SFTP outage to validate retry/backoff and retry limit alerts.
Cross-region tests: ensure records with residency=EU are excluded from US-only packages and vice-versa.
Performance: generate packages with synthetic 5M records to validate chunking and memory behavior.
deployment_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): enable feature flag for 3 internal tenants and run nightly scheduled packages for 2 weeks.
Phase 2: open to selected pilot customers with customer-managed KMS option behind a separate flag.
Phase 3: GA with UI surfaced in Console and API endpoints documented; monitor cost & error metrics for 30 days.
Rollback: disable scheduler ingestion and mark in-progress jobs as failed with retry disabled; keep generated artifacts for 7 days for forensic analysis.
